clue.text: Sacked a politician as a danger to miners

parts.note: to be sacked is to be fired from a job
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A dismissed politician is branded a menace to the mining community.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is explosive methane gas found in coal mines, a long-feared hazard underground.

clue.text: Complete a form to get a tankful of petrol

explanation.surface: Paperwork must be done before getting fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill up a form is to complete it; a fill-up is a full tank of fuel at the pump.

clue.text: Frustrated desire to live somewhere

indicators.note: a frustrated plan is thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A thwarted longing to settle down in a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell or have one's home in a place.

clue.text: Commission president led up to alternatives

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word led is read from bottom to top

parts.note: or is the word introducing alternatives, so several are ors

explanation.surface: A Commission president led the way to other options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LED into DEL. Jacques Delors was President of the European Commission 1985-95.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Delors headed the European Commission for a decade.

clue.text: Make space to resite churchyard memorial maybe

explanation.surface: Clearing room by relocating a grave monument.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MOVE A CROSS, the second part describes shifting a gravestone cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift sideways frees up room; relocating a crucifix-shaped headstone is the literal reading.

clue.text: Fiasco is the reason for some crowing going on

definitions.text: the reason for some crowing going on

explanation.surface: A disaster explains why a lot of gloating is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half literally: a cock being up and about is why the crowing happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock-up is slang for a botched job or mess; a rooster that is up crows at dawn.

clue.text: Like a wrestler floored and hauled up

explanation.surface: A grappler is thrown down and then dragged up.
explanation.walkthrough: To be on the mat is also to be reprimanded, from soldiers brought before an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler pinned down lies on the canvas; to be hauled up is to be called to account.

clue.text: Opening payment by a tenant?

parts.note: looks like a first instalment of rent, but means a sum paid to receive the means of unlocking the door

explanation.surface: A tenant makes an initial payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Key money is a premium a tenant pays to a landlord to be granted the lease.

clue.text: Left on a ship on the Suez Canal, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the answer sounds like what is described rather than being spelt that way

parts.note: Port Said is the Egyptian city at the northern end of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: A vessel moored on the Suez Canal, positioned to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The left-hand side of a vessel, facing forward, is called port.

clue.text: Failed completely on court and in courting

explanation.surface: Someone loses badly at tennis and also has no luck in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis 'love' means nil, so losing a set six-love is losing without scoring; in romance it is a former sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: At tennis to lose to love is to be whitewashed; in courtship it names a relationship that has ended.

clue.text: A later of corsets who lasts the course

explanation.surface: A corsetmaker turns out to have real endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are the old name for corsets, so one making them is a stay-er; a horse or runner with stamina is also a stayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays were stiffened bodices, so their maker is jokingly a stay-er; in racing a horse with stamina over distance is one.

clue.text: Subterranean passage in the course of construction

explanation.surface: A tunnel is still being built.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a road below ground; as an idiom it means already in progress.

clue.text: He spawns brave sons

parts.note: roes are the masses of fish eggs, or spawn

explanation.surface: A father produces courageous boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous men and boys are the champions celebrated for their valour.

clue.text: The Manx Tourist Trophy is for Manxmen

explanation.surface: A motorcycle event is held for the people of the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man; the Manx are also an island people.
explanation.definitionFit: The TT is a road race held on an island; a people living on an island are a nation of islanders.

clue.text: Urge a principal way to continue making progress

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
a head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A head teacher is pushed to keep moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to keep advancing despite obstacles.

clue.text: Caledonian news chief is thwarted

parts.note: Caledonia is the old name for Scotland, so Caledonian means Scotch
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A Scottish newspaper boss is frustrated.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to put an end to it, so it is foiled.

clue.text: Send a letter to cancel a bad debt

explanation.surface: Writing to someone to forgive an unpaid sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off is to dash off a letter, and also to accept an unrecoverable loss in the accounts.

clue.text: Set off for school in time

indicators.note: the school name is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving for school on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing, but means explode a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode.

clue.text: Books to chew over at the end of the back row

definitions.text: Books to chew over at the end of the back row

parts.words: Books to chew over at the end of the back row
parts.note: suggests a reader in a cinema or library, but describes a place you might reserve at the far end of the last row of seats

explanation.surface: Someone sits at the far end of the rear row with reading matter to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is the verb reserve: you book the spot at the end of a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat at the end of a row is in the angle of the room, the spot many prefer to reserve.

clue.text: Vedic psalm elevating art in support of humanity

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the turned word comes below the first
in a down clue raising the word art means it is read upwards

explanation.surface: A Hindu hymn lifts art in the service of mankind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevating' turns ART into TRA, which sits under MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred verse or chant from the Vedas, the ancient Hindu scriptures.

clue.text: Alabama beauty queen writing book for the masses

parts.note: a beauty pageant winner is titled Miss, as in Miss World
AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A pageant winner from Alabama writes a popular book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the masses' means Catholic services, not ordinary people; MISS goes before AL in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the prayers and texts of the Mass.

clue.text: Come to a sober conclusion

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so not drinking

explanation.surface: Coming to a soberly reasoned decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to' looks like waking up, but means be present at.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it, to turn up.

clue.text: Army mark end of day by beating it

definitions.text: end of day by beating it

explanation.surface: Soldiers bear a mark and finish the day with a drumming.
explanation.walkthrough: A tattoo is an inked mark popular with soldiers, and also the evening drum or bugle call recalling troops to quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are famous for inked skin designs; the evening drumbeat calling troops back to barracks has the same name.

clue.text: Maybe a Utopian schedule of proposals

explanation.surface: A dreamer draws up a list of plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A Utopian believes in perfect societies, a visionary; split in two the word is a list of ideas.

clue.text: Cheer the ebullient Henry

explanation.surface: An exuberant chap called Henry gives a shout of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hooray Henry is British slang for a loud, upper-class young man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a shout of joy, and the first word of the slang label for a brash posh young man.

clue.text: Vulgarity which makes one pull a face

definitions.text: which makes one pull a face

explanation.surface: Something crude causes a grimace.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgarity is a lack of refinement; a nasty flavour in the mouth also makes you grimace.

clue.text: Dim-wit ruffed out of order

indicators.note: letters not in their proper sequence are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool wearing a ruff is out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffer is an incompetent or stupid person.

clue.text: Assigned a job given full instructions

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a task with comprehensive briefing.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail a soldier is to assign them a duty; detailed instructions are thorough and complete.
